source_record.bounded_interface_domain: The exact shared item, configuration, time horizon, population and actually used receiving premise in the member are identified. source_record.domain_horizon_authority: Each exact object in the member, with actual horizon and decision rights established rather than presumed from the lineage label.
source_record.evidence_ceiling: Conditional analytical receiving consequence; no whole-predicate entailment, empirical net benefit, universal supplier rule, current legal determination or new historical descent.
source_record.native_common_basis: Critical item/site dependencies are known at the relevant time and actual substitution/recovery is distinguished from mere visibility.
source_record.common_cost_and_alternative: Mapping, confidential disclosure, updates and alternative qualification count. Low-criticality replaceable inputs can use a short register and actual replacement test.
attempted_contrary_interfaces: First-tier diversity treated as independent lower-tier supply.
A complete document treated as operational capability.
A partial exposure or criterion input rejected for failing the whole receiver.
Capacity, stock or staff double-counted for routine and contingency use.
Buyer savings treated as joint fair gain.

positive_controls.argument: The actual item/site dependency and substitution conditions can reveal hidden coupling or a common supplier assumption the interface contract must expose.
Dependency concentration, qualified substitution and restoration lead time inform whether the option is actually preservable before the next commitment.
Item/site identity and shared lower-tier dependence change the disruption scenarios and expose false diversification in the forecast.
Critical multi-tier information identifies who and what can block delivery and allows contingency and data obligations to follow the actual dependency.
A current critical-dependency map and actual recovery options expose a support or supply assumption that can invalidate a readiness claim.
Identifying shared sites, long restoration paths and qualified alternates supplies a concrete dependency premise or defeater for the recovery claim.
Current critical dependency and replacement information identifies obsolescence and supplier concentration that can undermine the support plan.
Specific lower-tier coupling, restoration delay and lack of qualified alternatives inform consequence and recovery dimensions of the control choice.
